items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: Now, you take, well, we'd call them the Zulu band. They had a hot brass band, see? Black Benny, myself, Lewis, and what does Tramon play our name? Eddie Morris.

ctx.x: Back to those brass bands here. Well, the Silverleaf brass band, they wouldn't really be playing too much music then, huh? No. Well. They'd be faking a lot of it, huh? Yeah.

Silverleaf had some good musicians. Tuxedo had some good musicians. Now, you take, well, we'd call them the Zulu band. They had a hot brass band, see? Black Benny, myself, Lewis, and what does Tramon play our name? Eddie Morris. Not Eddie Morris. Morris. Morris. Morris French. Morris French played Tramon with Rene. Yeah. items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: Tick, Black Benny, Lewis, and myself, and Henry Martin... we come back playing the blues

ctx.x: Did you see any changes in the brass bands from the time you got here to the time you left, say, 1919 to 1940?

Well, yeah, from what I can see, Tick, Black Benny, Lewis, and myself, and Henry Martin. Yeah. And some of them did change it while I was here. And after one big parade one day, we come back playing, you know, the blues stuff on the street. They didn't play blues on the street. Henry, and then Rosino decided to play some blues, play them fast, you know. Henry who? Henry Martin, I mean, not Henry Rosino.
